# Graph-first v2 (graph with api + repr + decision layers, contracts generated by script)

Graph v2: 572 nodes / 1632 edges (api 124, repr 33, decision 82). Contracts: generated mechanically by `contract/gen_contracts.py` from graph.json (10 files). 8 coders in parallel (1587 lines total), contract only.

## Results (116 rule tests + legacy 164)
- Only test-facing NAME aliases added in evaluation (names not fixed by given code: certificate_limit, certificate_count, _face_value, compute_operating_order, stock_round_order, start_operating_round_set, final_wealth, final_standings). No behaviour/default/protocol adapters.
- Rule tests: 113 passed / 3 failed (v1 graph: 86 with names only, 105 with extra diagnostic adapters).
- The 3: 5.12.13 stock-market arrows (given code, out of scope); 4.1.2 priority holder not used as first player in start_stock_round (representation: v2 uses player_order[0]); 4.11.9 `reorder_players_by_cash` mutates and returns None (test expects the list).
- Legacy tests: 138 passed / 18 failed (test_trains cannot import `current_buyable_pool`, not in graph). ~9 failures are sandbox artifacts (missing docs/frontend files); rest are legacy-vs-ruling conflicts (R6b, 4.4.3, 4.5.2, certificate limit incl P16...).
- Previously failing train, private-revenue (3.1.2) and arrow-free rules now pass: trains/phase/rust/limit, concession/private revenue.
## Takeaway
Adding interface/representation/decision nodes to the graph removed the interface-level failures of v1 (30 -> 3). Remaining failures are naming/return-type conventions the graph cannot know without a consumer, plus out-of-scope given code.
Caveats: single run; graph builder saw GAPS.md derived from earlier failing runs (indirect tuning); owner-needed decisions (11 `needs_owner`) are provisional; R6b provisional.
